Tall all-powerful Rama, in his astonishment, bowed low to that

since that Lord of the Titans mer with no resistance, or had the

Mahishmati which rivalled that of the Gods, where the Deity of 
Fire dwelt perpctuslly. 
There a monarch reigned, named 
Arjuna, in effulgence like unto the fire which was kept there ever 
concealed in a pit covered by reeds.' 
" On that day, the powerful Sovereign of the Haihayas, Lord 
Arjuna went to the River Narmada to sport with his wives and

most powerful of monarchs. Do you announce mine arrival to 
him!'

the son of Vishravas learning from the people of the city that

brief.summary_1line: Ravana arrives at Mahishmati seeking King Arjuna, travels to the Vindhya and Narmada, and pauses in admiration of the river’s beauty.

image_candidates.scene_text: Ravana stands on the sandy banks of the Narmada after descending from the Pushpaka chariot, gazing over the lotus-filled river beneath the Vindhya mountains.
The Vindhya range rises with cloud-like peaks, waterfalls crashing down while celestial beings and animals roam its forests.
Ravana seated on the riverbank with his ministers, the golden sunset reflecting on the Narmada as birds and beasts gather at the water.
